title: FACT CHECK: Trump did not praise Davao City’s energy security efforts
summary: Reports from news outlets quoted the US leader saying, ‘We have more energy than any country in the world by double.’ The misleading posts misinterpret ‘double’ as ‘Davao.’

blocks.text: Claim: US President Donald Trump praised Davao City for its energy security efforts.

Why we fact-checked this: A Facebook reel bearing the claim was posted by the page Baste Duterte fan on November 21. The video has received 76,000 views, 1,700 reactions, 517 shares, and 139 comments as of writing.
The video shows Trump in a bilateral talk with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on November 18.

Text overlaid on the video reads, “[Number one] energy save security Davao City in the world.” The post further claimed that Marcos was supposedly taken aback when he heard Trump mention Davao City, the stronghold of his political rivals, the Dutertes.
Another Facebook reel, which has already garnered an estimated 704,000 views, also claimed that the US government will provide Davao City with a new energy project.

The facts: Nowhere in Trump’s statements during the bilateral talks did he say that Davao City was number one in the world for its energy security efforts. He also did not mention any new US government energy project for the city. No global rankings or news reports identify Davao City as a top city for energy conservation and security, contrary to the claim.

Reports from news outlets such as GMA News quoted Trump saying, “We have more energy than any country in the world by double.” The misleading post misinterpreted Trump’s pronunciation of “double” as “Davao.”

Trump was actually referring to US energy production. He claimed that the country is now the leading producer of oil and natural gas, surpassing the combined supply of Russia and Saudi Arabia, with the US leader also referencing its “acquisition” of Venezuela’s oil reserves. Trump also said the US aims to increase energy exports to Pacific allies, including the Philippines.

Trade deal: The posts circulated following Trump’s arrival in Manila on November 17 for a state visit and to participate in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations-US Special Summit, as well as the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue leaders’ summit.

During his visit, the US leader highlighted what he described as the “biggest trade deal” between the Philippines and the United States. The US is strengthening its defense partnership with the Philippines while signaling interest in expanding cooperation on energy security, particularly in nuclear energy.

US energy production: Trump’s remarks appeared to refer primarily to the United States’ energy production, particularly oil and natural gas. He has previously made the claim that the US is producing more oil and gas “than Russia and Saudi Arabia combined.” According to an article by PolitiFact, this remark is “mostly true,” but added that the US lead over the two countries “is built on the other liquids, not crude oil.”

According to Our World in Data, a project by UK-based nonprofit Global Change Data Lab, when considering total energy supply across different sources, including coal, oil, natural gas, renewables, and nuclear energy, China ranks first globally, with approximately 45,000 terawatt-hours in 2025.
